Sector labels are placed near their respective data points for easy identification, providing clarity on the trade dynamics between the two regions. The grid lines and contrasting colors enhance readability, allowing for a clear comparison of trade metrics across different sectors. The chart effectively highlights how certain sectors dominate trade either by value, volume, or economic significance, offering a comprehensive view of Liberia-North Africa trade relations in 2023.

p = Path("chart.py")
src = p.read_text()
for group in ("export", "import"):
    src = src.replace(
        f"[x[1] for x in {group}_data],\n    [x[0] for x in {group}_data],",
        f"[x[0] for x in {group}_data],\n    [x[1] for x in {group}_data],"
    )
src = src.replace("c='#e15759'", "c='TEMP'").replace("c='#4e79a7'", "c='#e15759'").replace("c='TEMP'", "c='#4e79a7'")
src = src.replace("South America-Europe Trade", "Liberia-North Africa Trade")
p.write_text(src)
exec(compile(src, "chart.py", "exec"))
ax = plt.gca()
print("Title:", ax.get_title())
print("Limits:", ax.get_xlim(), ax.get_ylim())
for coll, kind in zip(ax.collections, ["Export", "Import"]):
    sub = df[df.Trade_Type == kind]
    import numpy as np
    assert np.allclose(coll.get_offsets(), sub[["Trade_Value_Millions", "Trade_Volume_Thousands"]].to_numpy())
    assert np.allclose(coll.get_sizes(), sub.Economic_Impact_Score.to_numpy()*15)
    print(kind, "color:", coll.get_facecolors()[0], "points:", len(coll.get_offsets()))
print("Legend:", ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1])
